findings_to_judge.finding: US energy storage installed a record 20.2 GWh in calendar Q2 2026 (17.9-18.0 GWh utility-scale, 1.8 GWh commercial/industrial), 30.8 GWh in H1, and SEIA/Benchmark RAISED the full-year 2026 forecast to 71 GWh versus 59 GWh installed in 2025 - published 2026-09-01, twelve weeks after ABM last spoke, and covering the two months (May, June) that sit inside ABM's fiscal Q3.

CBRE's Q2 2026 US office report (2026-07-29) shows national vacancy falling 30bp to 18.3% - 'the largest quarterly decline since 2015' - net absorption of 12.6m sq ft, nearly double the prior quarter and a ninth straight positive quarter, leasing +16% y/y, with CBRE projecting 2026 annual leasing to surpass the 2022 record; San Francisco, the exact market ABM's CEO singled out on 2026-06-05 as having vacancy 'probably 2 or 3x worse than New York City', posted +963,980 sq ft of net absorption in the quarter.

ABM Aviation grew 19.5% in Q2 and its CEO warned on 2026-06-05 that 'rising fuel costs will likely create some near-term challenges for our airline clients'; since then the airline cost shock deepened rather than resolved - American Airlines cut FY26 guidance a second time in July (to a -$0.65 to +$0.65 adjusted EPS range from -$0.40 to +$1.10, with a Q3 loss guide, on ~$3.75/gal fuel), Southwest cut FY26 to $3.25-$4.25 from 'at least $4' after a ~$900m y/y Q2 fuel increase, and Alaska has had guidance suspended since April.

Note 8 of the Q2 FY26 10-Q states that ABM performed its review of the majority of its casualty insurance programmes during Q2 2026 and 'it was determined that there was no adjustment required for our total reserves related to prior years during the six months ended April 30, 2026' - so the item that produced a $(22.2)m pre-tax hit (~100bp of adjusted EBITDA margin, ~$0.26/sh) in Q4 FY25 is a Q2/Q4 event and is very unlikely to appear in the Q3 print, even though ABM's adjusted EPS definition now includes it while its guidance range is stated 'before any impact from prior-year self-insurance adjustments'.
